verdict.rationale: Browser Use's first-party authentication guide documents profiles that persist cookies, local storage, and login state across browsers. The documented flow is to log in once, save the profile, and reuse it so future browsers start already logged in. The 2FA guide also names a saved profile as one of the most reliable options. Missing for 10: API-level detail on creating and attaching profiles to runs, and independent hands-on corroboration of cloud profile reuse.

support.subject: As a developer, I can persist logged-in browser state in reusable profiles so agents skip the login wall on every subsequent run

citations.quote: A profile persists cookies, local storage, and login state across browsers.
Log in once, save the profile, then reuse it to start future browsers already logged in.
The most reliable options are a saved profile or a human checkpoint.
